method.label: Maximize the sum of the factors

annotationRationale: Factoring the square difference and enforcing parity restricts the integer roots. A universal bound on the factor sum, together with an attaining pair, proves the maximum.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official difference-of-squares and same-parity factor-pair method. Divides both factors by 2 and supplies an explicit inequality proving that the extreme factor pair maximizes k.

review.mathCheck: Same-parity factors of 2560 must both be even, giving positive integers \(ab=640\) and \(k=a+b\). Since \((a-1)(b-1)\ge0\), \(k\le641\), attained with \((a,b)=(1,640)\). Then \(j=639\) and \(M=407108\), whose units digit is 8, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded refinement of MAA Q15's first approach on pages 8 and 9. It retains even-factor optimization and adds an elementary universal bound proving the official maximizing pair.
review.annotationCheck: The bound and attaining construction establish greatestness without enumerating every pair. Difference of squares, integer restrictions, and extremal reasoning are assessed; elementary parity appropriately supports them.
